title: Version Control with Git
learning_outcomes: Explain what version control with git contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: repositories and commits.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Production reliability includes repeatable builds, correct runtime configuration, secret separation, compatible migrations, health checks, logging, monitoring, and a rollback strategy—not only uploading source files. In this lesson, focus on repositories and commits; then compare it with branches and merges. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use version control with git when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production reliability includes repeatable builds, correct runtime configuration, secret separation, compatible migrations, health checks, logging, monitoring, and a rollback strategy—not only uploading source files. For version control with git, begin with repositories and commits. Also distinguish branches and merges; pull requests; code review. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Version Control with Git
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$release = ["test" => true, "migrate" => true, "deploy" => true, "health_check" => true];
echo count(array_filter($release)) . " checks enabled" . PHP_EOL;

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep secrets outside build artifacts, run repeatable checks before rollout, and define health checks and rollback plans.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for version control with git from top to bottom. Start by identifying repositories and commits, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.

hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.

summary: Version Control with Git is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Keep secrets outside build artifacts, run repeatable checks before rollout, and define health checks and rollback plans.
